title: Six verbes essentiels au subjonctif
summary: Use complete subjunctive paradigms of être, avoir, aller, faire, pouvoir and savoir.
objectives: Produce all persons of six high-frequency irregular verbs.
Keep subjunctive forms distinct from indicative and future forms.

sections.title: Être and avoir: learn the whole pattern
paragraphs: An auxiliary is a helping verb used to form a compound tense. Être and avoir also function on their own: to be and to have. Their subjunctives are essential both independently and later in the past subjunctive.

Neither verb follows the regular present-stem recipe. In aie, aies and aient, the final letters distinguish the persons even when they sound alike. Soyons, soyez, ayons and ayez contain y, not the regular -ions/-iez sequence.
points: Paradigms use je, tu, il/elle/on, nous, vous, ils/elles in that order.

examples.french:
que je **sois**
que tu **sois**
qu'il/elle/on **soit**
que nous **soyons**
que vous **soyez**
qu'ils/elles **soient**
examples.english:
that I be
that you be
that he/she/one be
that we be
that you be
that they be
examples.note: English subjunctive 'be' is shown to make the paradigm compact.

examples.french:
que j'**aie**
que tu **aies**
qu'il/elle/on **ait**
que nous **ayons**
que vous **ayez**
qu'ils/elles **aient**
examples.english:
that I have
that you have
that he/she/one have
that we have
that you have
that they have
examples.note: Do not confuse ait with est or aient with ont.

examples.english: She needs to have a copy.

mistakes.avoid: Il faut que vous soyiez prêts.
mistakes.prefer: Il faut que vous soyez prêts.
mistakes.why: The exceptional vous form is soyez.

sections.title: Aller changes stems; faire keeps fass-
paragraphs: Aller uses aill- in the singular and third-person plural, but all- for nous and vous. Faire uses fass- for every person. These are subjunctive stems: do not replace them with future ir- or fer-.

examples.french:
que j'**aille**
que tu **ailles**
qu'il/elle/on **aille**
que nous **allions**
que vous **alliez**
qu'ils/elles **aillent**
examples.english:
that I go
that you go
that he/she/one go
that we go
that you go
that they go
examples.note: Allions and alliez can also be imperfect indicative elsewhere; context identifies the mood.

examples.french:
que je **fasse**
que tu **fasses**
qu'il/elle/on **fasse**
que nous **fassions**
que vous **fassiez**
qu'ils/elles **fassent**
examples.english:
that I do/make
that you do/make
that he/she/one do/make
that we do/make
that you do/make
that they do/make
They need to go to the depot.

examples.french: Il faut que nous **allions** les chercher.
examples.english: We need to go and get them.

examples.french: Il faut que tu **fasses** une pause.
examples.english: You need to take a break.
examples.note: Faire une pause means take a break.

mistakes.why: The subjunctive stem of faire is fass-, not fais-.

sections.title: Pouvoir and savoir have stable exceptional stems
paragraphs: Pouvoir uses puiss- and savoir uses sach-, followed by the ordinary subjunctive endings. Pouvoir describes ability or permission; savoir describes knowledge or knowing how. Il faut que requires a subjunctive even when the skill or information is perfectly real.

examples.french:
que je **puisse**
que tu **puisses**
qu'il/elle/on **puisse**
que nous **puissions**
que vous **puissiez**
qu'ils/elles **puissent**
examples.english:
that I can
that you can
that he/she/one can
that we can
that you can
that they can
examples.note: English can has no matching visible subjunctive.

examples.french:
que je **sache**
que tu **saches**
qu'il/elle/on **sache**
que nous **sachions**
que vous **sachiez**
qu'ils/elles **sachent**
examples.english:
that I know
that you know
that he/she/one know
that we know
that you know
that they know
examples.note: Do not use the indicative sav- stem here.

examples.english: Everyone needs to be able to enter.
You need to know how to swim.
examples.note: Savoir + infinitive describes a learned skill.

practice.prompt: Present subjunctive of être only: Il faut que je ___ disponible.
Present subjunctive of avoir only: Il faut qu'ils ___ les clés.
Present subjunctive of aller only: Il faut que tu ___ au bureau.
Present subjunctive of faire only: Il faut que nous ___ un choix.
Present subjunctive of pouvoir only: Il faut que vous ___ lire l'écran.
Present subjunctive of savoir only: Il faut qu'elle ___ répondre.
Supply être in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'elles ___ présentes.
Supply avoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que tu ___ assez de temps.
Supply aller in the present subjunctive: Il faut que vous ___ à pied.
Supply faire in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'on ___ vite.
Supply pouvoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que nous ___ sortir.
Supply savoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'ils ___ où aller.
Supply avoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que j'___ une autorisation.
practice.explanation: Je has aie, without s or t.

practice.prompt: Supply être in the present subjunctive: Il faut que nous ___ attentifs.
Supply aller in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'elle ___ voir le gardien.
Supply faire in the present subjunctive: Il faut que vous ___ moins de bruit.
Supply pouvoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut qu'ils ___ se reposer.
Supply savoir in the present subjunctive: Il faut que tu ___ mon adresse.

production_task.prompt: A colleague is preparing a first aid workshop. Write four requirements with il faut que and four of this lesson's verbs. Explain who needs which resource or ability.
production_task.model_answer: Il faut que la salle soit calme. Il faut que nous ayons une trousse de secours. Il faut que vous fassiez une démonstration. Il faut que tous les participants puissent voir vos gestes.
production_task.translation: The room needs to be quiet. We need to have a first aid kit. You need to give a demonstration. All the participants need to be able to see your movements.
rubric: Four different target verbs have correct stems and person endings.
Each requirement names a clear subject.
The requirements fit the workshop context.
Avoir and être are chosen for meaning, not simply because both are irregular.
